neutral_facts.value: The accused and the victim were relatives with a common ancestor. The incident began when the victim's cattle strayed into the fields of the accused and destroyed crops, leading to abuse from the accused. Later, an altercation occurred between the victim and the accused while they were sitting in their compounds. The accused, under exhortation, brought a gun and fired at the victim, who was then assaulted with lathis. The victim died on the spot. The prosecution presented eyewitness accounts and medical evidence showing the victim had firearm wounds and other injuries, while the accused also had minor injuries. The High Court concluded that the accused did not have a criminal background and that the incident occurred without premeditation, leading to a conviction under Section 304 Part I with a reduced sentence.

prosecution_argument.value: The prosecution argued that the accused persons formed an unlawful assembly and jointly launched a lethal attack on the deceased using a firearm, resulting in his death. The incident occurred after a series of altercations between the deceased and the accused persons, leading to the deceased being shot and assaulted.

defence_argument.value: The defence argued that the prosecution failed to prove that the accused persons were the aggressors who assaulted the deceased, and that the deceased and his cohorts attacked the accused persons, prompting the accused to defend themselves with a firearm. They also claimed that there was no pre-meditation or prior concert on the part of the accused persons.
